merger_name: Goodstart – certain Edge Early Learning centres (in administration)

targets.name: EDGE EARLY LEARNING HOLDINGS PTY LTD

party_page.name: Edge Early Learning Holdings Pty Ltd

merger_description:
Goodstart Early Learning Ltd (**Goodstart**) proposes to acquire the business and assets of 31 childcare centres operated by Edge Early Learning Holdings Pty Ltd (Administrators Appointed) (**Edge**) (the **Acquisition**).

Goodstart is a national provider of early learning and childcare services, operating a network of 666 childcare centres across Australia. Goodstart is a not-for-profit provider formed by The Benevolent Society, Mission Australia, the Brotherhood of St Laurence and Social Ventures Australia.

Edge is an Australian early childhood education provider which operates a network of 64 childcare centres across Queensland and South Australia. Edge is in administration and the Acquisition will take place following a sale process conducted by the Administrators.

Both Goodstart and Edge provide centre-based childcare and early childhood education services (**long day care**) for children aged 0-6 years in relevant local areas in Queensland and South Australia. This includes kindergarten and preschool programs where applicable.

The parties have entered into a Heads of Agreement which provides the terms on which Goodstart will acquire the assets and business of the relevant Edge childcare centres, including leasehold interests, plant and equipment, contracts, and regulatory approvals.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
other relevant information available to it. The ACCC has also had
regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition because:
a. in respect of 23 target Edge long day care centres, there is
no geographic overlap between the target centre and any
existing Goodstart centre in the relevant local areas
• b. in respect of the remaining 8 target Edge long day care
centres where there is geographic overlap between the
target centre and an existing Goodstart centre, Goodstart
would face competition from multiple alternative providers
of long day care services in the local area post-Acquisition
c. absent the Acquisition, some of the target Edge centres may
otherwise close, reducing or removing consumers’ access to
long day care services in the relevant local areas.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition and continuity of service for essential childcare
services.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
